newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says will be candidate for Tory leadership.
newsitem.headline: Clarke says will be candidate for Tory leadership.

text.p: Former British Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke said he would be a candidate for the leadership of the Conservative party after its election defeat.
"I certainly intend to be a candidate in the leadership election," Clarke told BBC Radio Four, according to the Press Association news agency.
Clarke was the leading Europhile in the cabinet of outgoing Prime Minister John Major, who announced earlier that he would stand down as Conservative leader.
He said he had made no preparations for the leadership campaign and had no organisation, but planned to consult with friends. His leadership bid would not be based on the issue of Europe, he added.

Clarke's unashamedly pro-European views, which he stubbornly refused to tone down in the face of massive pressure from the Conservative party's powerful Euro-sceptics, often put him at odds with mainstream party thinking.
Last year, he said it would be "complete folly" to rule out British participation in a single currency and "pathetic" if Britain waited to see how monetary union developed before making up its mind.
